body:
### Describe the bug

Since #7489, `runtests.py` adds `('CYTHON_REFNANNY', '1')` to `CDEFS` in `setup_test_directory()` ([runtests.py#L3023-L3033](https://github.com/cython/cython/blob/d1bb620811b0cf7e9f3fe4fb77ccb3d40a38f6c0/runtests.py#L3023-L3033)), which only runs in the main process. Before, `runtests()` added it in every test process. With `-jN`, the tests run in the worker processes of a `ProcessPoolExecutor`, and these only inherit `CDEFS` if they are forked. The default start method is `forkserver` on Linux since Python 3.14, and `spawn` on macOS and Windows, so the workers compile every test without `CYTHON_REFNANNY` and refnanny checks nothing.

`Tools/ci-run.sh` runs `runtests.py -j7`, so since February the CI jobs on Linux with Python 3.14 and later (including the limited API, shared utility, module state and type specs jobs on 3.14) and all macOS and Windows jobs have run without reference count checking. Only the Linux jobs on Python 3.13 and older still have it.

The `--debug-*` options of `runtests.py` are lost in the workers in the same way (this part is older than #7489): `main()` sets them on `DebugFlags` in the main process only. With `--debug-trace-code-generation`, the C file of the test below has 24 trace comments with `-j1` and none with `-j2` on 3.14.

### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

A test that reports whether it was compiled with `CYTHON_REFNANNY`:

```cython
# tests/run/refnanny_probe.pyx
cdef extern from *:
    const bint CYTHON_REFNANNY

def compiled_with_refnanny():
    """
    >>> compiled_with_refnanny()
    True
    """
    return CYTHON_REFNANNY
```

```
$ python3.14 runtests.py --no-code-style --backends=c -j1 refnanny_probe
...
OK
$ python3.14 runtests.py --no-code-style --backends=c -j2 refnanny_probe
...
Failed example:
    compiled_with_refnanny()
Expected:
    True
Got:
    False
```

Results on Linux with GitHub's CPython builds and master at d1bb62081:

| Python | default start method | `-j1` | `-j2` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.13.18t | fork | True | True |
| 3.14.10 | forkserver | True | **False** (True with `multiprocessing.set_start_method("fork")`) |
| 3.14.10t | forkserver | True | **False** (True with `fork`) |
| 3.15.2 | forkserver | True | **False** |
| 3.15.2t | forkserver | True | **False** |

The binaries agree: `strings refnanny_probe*.so | grep -c RefNannyAPI` gives 1 for the `-j1` build and 0 for the `-j2` build.

So real leaks pass unnoticed. The `break` leak of #8156, which is not fixed on master yet:

```cython
# tests/run/cs_break_leak.pyx
cimport cython

def leave_with_break(obj):
    """
    >>> leave_with_break(object())
    """
    while True:
        with cython.critical_section(obj):
            break
```

On 3.14, `-j1` fails with `REFNANNY: References leaked:` in `leave_with_break()`, while `-j2` passes.

The same thing without Cython:

```python
import multiprocessing
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor

CDEFS = []

def worker_cdefs(_):
    return CDEFS

if __name__ == '__main__':
    CDEFS.append(('CYTHON_REFNANNY', '1'))   # as setup_test_directory() does
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(1) as pool:
        print(multiprocessing.get_start_method(), pool.submit(worker_cdefs, 0).result())
```

prints `fork [('CYTHON_REFNANNY', '1')]` on 3.13 and `forkserver []` on 3.14 and 3.15.

### Expected behaviour

Every test process compiles the tests with `CYTHON_REFNANNY`, whatever the start method, unless refnanny is off (`--no-refnanny`, PyPy, GraalPy). The `--debug-*` options apply in every test process too.

### OS

Linux. macOS and Windows by code inspection (`spawn` is their default start method).

### Python version

3.14.10, 3.14.10t, 3.15.2, 3.15.2t (3.13.18t is not affected)

### Cython version

master at d1bb62081, and 3.3.x since 3.3.0a1

### Additional context

I noticed this while testing #8157. PR #8159 (https://github.com/cython/cython/pull/8159) adds the define in `runtests()` again and passes the `--debug-*` options on to the workers. With it, refnanny reports no errors in the existing tests on Linux: the full suite (C and C++) on 3.14 and 3.14t, the module state and limited API runs on 3.14, and 3.15 and 3.15t (C). So restoring the checks shouldn't turn the Linux jobs red. I couldn't test macOS and Windows.

title: [BUG] `runtests.py -jN` compiles the tests without refnanny on Python 3.14+, macOS and Windows
